IncidentBot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate (503) from okta-edge on /introspect (region: us-east) — threshold breached for 6m. Paging oncall: @Ben. https://incidents.internal/alerts/okta-edge-503s
Ben: ack — I'm on it. seeing spike starting ~1719812200. console login errors also reported from web-frontend. will triage.
Mia: oncall handover? Ben, do you want me to jump in? I can run a quick aggregation of errors by client_id and region.
Ben: yes please. Mia, can you check token verification vs introspect failures? also check if JWKS fetch errors are present.
Mia: running quick query:
```
SELECT count(*) as errs, error_type, client_id, region FROM auth.logs
WHERE ts > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND code IN (401,403,429,502,503)
GROUP BY error_type, client_id, region
ORDER BY errs DESC
```
Mia: results — top 3: 503 introspect timeout (us-east, client-app-frontend) ~420 errs, 401 token-verify signature-fail (us-east) ~120 errs, 429 introspect-rate-limit (us-east) ~90 errs. overall ~11% failed logins across web-console traffic.
Diego: I opened a support ticket with Okta, ticket OKTA-987654. Okta status page shows "degraded performance for US Edge cluster" — engineering says they're investigating.
Carla: support queue: 8 active tickets calling out SSO login fails, 3 are enterprise customers reporting console locked. customers asking if this is inside Redwood or Okta. need a status blurb.
Raj: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable local JWKS validation fallback to avoid introspect for known long-lived tokens; 2) increase JWKS cache TTL and serve cached keys on fetch errors; 3) throttle our introspect fanout to backoff and queue requests to avoid amplifying Okta load. I can prepare a quick hotfix.
Ben: sounds good. Mia, can you confirm which services call introspect frequently? I want to avoid breaking expected flows.
Mia: looks like auth-proxy and session-service spawn most introspects. session-service does a fanout for each web request currently if no cache hit.
Raj: patch ready — small config toggle. deploying to prod can be done with env flips:
```
# reduce introspect fanout and enable jwks local fallback
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/session-service INTROSPECT_FANOUT=1
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-proxy JWKS_FALLBACK=local
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-proxy JWKS_CACHE_TTL=3600
```
Ben: deploying those now. pushing as a canary to 4 pods then 100% if green.
Ben: canary done. monitoring.
Mia: initial metrics: introspect call rate down 68%, 503 rate to Okta dropping. token-verify 401s falling too. console error rate down from 11% -> 3.2% in 6 minutes. :raised_hands:
Diego: Okta responded: "We're seeing an upstream network congestion affecting edge cluster in us-east. Mitigations are in progress. We recommend reducing introspect rate and using local verification where possible." They gave ETA ~45m.
Carla: sending status update to affected customers now: "We are investigating SSO failures to Okta affecting console logins in us-east. We've applied temporary mitigations to reduce retries and use cached keys; some customers may see intermittent successful logins. We'll update again in 30 minutes."
Claire: capturing customer impact + comms. please paste the support ticket links and list of affected customer ids. I'll coordinate external messaging.
Mia: affected client_ids (top): enterprise-42, partner-alpha, internal-admin. I've added a temp ACL that avoids re-auth for internal-admin for 30m to unblock support.
Raj: rolling the config to 100%. also disabled healthcheck-triggered introspects (healthcheck -> skip_introspect=true).
Ben: after 25m from mitigation, total login failures now ~1.1%, still elevated but much improved. continuing to monitor.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-23109 (high) — okta-edge-introspect-deg. Initial responders: Ben, Mia. Link: https://pagerduty.internal/incidents/PD-23109
Diego: Okta posted status update: mitigating, partial recovery starting. their post: "reducing edge SSL termination concurrency; routing changes underway".
Mia: logging note: saved config snapshot and commands used in runbook:
```
# snapshot
kubectl -n prod get deploy session-service -o yaml > /tmp/session-service.prehotfix.yaml
# applied env changes
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/session-service INTROSPECT_FANOUT=1
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-proxy JWKS_FALLBACK=local JWKS_CACHE_TTL=3600
```
Ben: handing off for long-running followup to Raj (eng-runtime) and Claire (product/customer comms). I'll be offcall in 20m. escalation doc: https://confluence.internal/incidents/1719812345-okta-edge-introspect
Raj: I'll own post-incident tasks: add rate-limiting around introspect callers, add circuit-breaker for external introspect, add a more robust JWKS cache with warm-start on deploy.
Carla: will follow up with affected customers and escalate any P1s.
Claire: thanks — I'll prepare a public-facing status note once Okta confirms full recovery.
Ben: thanks team — great quick work. reactions: :white_check_mark: :coffee: :eyes:
IncidentBot: Incident status: investigating -> mitigated (temporary) — next update scheduled in 30m."
